subject: Incubator credit structure: rollover, clawback, and engagement bonus proposal
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@seedfoundry.com>, Ada Labs <apply@adalabs.org>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incubator credit structure: rollover, clawback, and engagement bonus proposal

Hi Samir (and Ada Labs team),

Thanks for the time on Friday — appreciate the follow-up. I pulled together a proposal for how we could structure the startup credits and a small engagement incentive so the cohort sees predictable runway without creating undue billing complexity for you. High level:

- Stipend + Usage Pool: $5k one-time stipend per accepted startup, plus a shared usage pool of $25k per cohort (applied at the org level).
- Rollover window: unused stipend funds can roll into a cohort-level overage buffer for 60 days after cohort end.
- Clawback safeguard: if a startup is inactive for >90 days without responding to outreach or hitting a minimal engagement metric (1 demo or 2 API calls/day average in the first 30 days), we reserve the right to reclaim rolled funds and reallocate to new cohort members.
- Engagement bonus: additional $1k in credits for startups that hit the engagement checklist (demo scheduled + 3 distinct engineers onboarded + 5000 tokens consumed within 30 days).

Attached are the draft program terms (program_terms_v2.pdf) and a sample usage snapshot from Q1 (usage_snapshot_q1.csv) so you can see how consumption typically tails off after week 4.

Can you share any constraints from your finance team around clawback language? We want to avoid legal friction while keeping the program sustainable. Ben and Marissa — copying you for visibility on pricing impact and ops.

Next step: if this looks reasonable, I can convert into a short MOU and loop in your legal team.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

https://redwood.com

Subject: Re: Incubator credit structure: rollover, clawback, and engagement bonus proposal

Thanks Dylan — this is helpful and very concrete. A few quick questions from our side:

1) Clawback timing: 90 days sounds fair but can we make the reallocation subject to a 14-day notice and an outreach attempt log? We typically push back on any automatic reclaim without documented outreach.
2) Rollover visibility: can we get a per-startup dashboard (or CSV) showing remaining stipend so we can proactively reassign credits before the 60-day cutoff?
3) Tax / accounting: some of our partners treat credits as a grant; our finance folks want language clarifying that credits are prepaid service credits (so they don't get treated as income).

Also — curious if you can do a small pilot tweak: for the first 10 startups in the May cohort, allow unused stipends to convert into a 40% overage discount (instead of returning to Redwood). It would help us smooth transitions for very early-stage teams.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to close. Samir
Founder & Program Director | Seed Foundry
M: +1 917-555-2121

Dylan / team — quick internal take from pricing:

- The engagement bonus is a good incentive and low-cost if we gate it on measurable telemetry. Recommend adding telemetry ID checks (first API key rotation + two distinct IPs) to prevent gaming.
- The pilot request (convert unused stipends to 40% overage discount for first 10 startups) is doable but needs clear cutover rules: define "unused" as <10% consumption of stipend at cohort end.
- Clawback with 14-day notice: ok, but finance will want the right to clawback only to the extent credits are unused and unbilled — we should avoid any language implying reclamation of actual cash.

Lauren, pls confirm whether we can produce the per-startup stipend CSV export on a weekly cadence (we have that in our billing API now).

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incubator credit structure: rollover, clawback, and engagement bonus proposal

Ben is correct — we can generate a per-startup stipend export on a weekly schedule. Operational notes:

- CSV will include startup name, startup id, stipend_allocated_usd, stipend_used_usd, stipend_remaining_usd, last_activity_date (UTC).
- For clawback, finance requires: documented outreach (email log), 14-day notice, and a manual approval from Revenue Ops for any reallocation. We cannot auto-charge or force a refund of credits that have been invoiced.
- Accounting note: we classify promotional credits as contra-revenue (not taxable income for recipients). Legal will still want a short clause clarifying status; include a short "no cash value" statement in the MOU to appease partners.

I can spin up the CSV export and a sample MOU clause if we want to present something to Seed Foundry next week.

Lauren Bishop
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Incubator credit structure: rollover, clawback, and engagement bonus proposal

Samir — thanks for the feedback and for the pilot idea. We're aligned on the principles and can offer the following narrowed proposal for the May cohort: 

1) May pilot (first 10 startups): unused stipend (<10% used at cohort end) can be converted into a 40% discount on overage for the following 60 days. We will cap aggregate converted discount at $10k per startup.
2) Rollover: stipends may roll to the cohort-level buffer for 60 days; any reallocation requires documented outreach and a 14-day notice.
3) Clawback: we will only reallocate unused, unbilled credits after notice and Revenue Ops approval; no cash clawbacks.
4) Engagement bonus: $1k credit awarded upon meeting the engagement checklist; gated by telemetry to ensure genuine usage.

If that works, Dylan will draft a one-page MOU and I'll have our legal/finance add the standard "no cash value" line. Can we schedule a 30-minute sync Friday to finalize?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partner Programs | Redwood Inference
